public_rationale: The deadline elapsed, but the stated condition failed under the ordinary each-company reading. The filing-based analysis reports that Tesla spent $8.527 billion in 2025, below both its initial plan above $11 billion and its April revision above $10 billion. The conditional forecast therefore cannot be scored as a success or failure. This does not establish whether the five-company totals exceeded $560 billion or produced about $35 billion of AI revenue.
limitations: The condition verdict relies on a traceable secondary source because primary filing reads failed.
Reading the condition as aggregate spending could change the adjudication.
Total capital spending is used only to test Tesla's spending promise, not as AI-only outcome evidence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If they keep their promises, by end of 2025 these five companies will have spent over $560 billion in AI capex over two years to earn around $35 billion in AI revenue.
conditions: if they keep their capex promises

statement.excerpt: If they keep their promises, by the end of 2025, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Tesla will have spent over $560 billion in capital expenditures on AI in the last two years, all to make around $35 billion.
statement.document_title: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

from_speaker: Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Tesla
our_interpretation: The plain reading of the condition is that each named company fulfills its spending plan in place when the post appeared. Other companies overspending does not replace an individual company's unmet plan.
The two-year outcome period is calendar 2024–2025, following the heading and year-end deadline.
Making around $35 billion means aggregate AI revenue over those two years, rather than profit or financing.
The contextual calculation combines company spending plans with press and analyst revenue estimates, so its composite accounting basis is estimate.
Around has no numerical tolerance. I do not invent a tolerance that determines the result.
The single metric_scope records the compound claim; expenditure and revenue must still be tested separately.
criteria.support_condition: The antecedent is met, and comparable evidence shows aggregate AI capital expenditures above USD 560 billion and approximately USD 35 billion of realized AI revenue across the five companies during calendar 2024–2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The antecedent is met, but comparable evidence establishes that either the expenditure threshold or the approximate revenue amount failed. Failure of the antecedent is not a failed forecast.

evidence.explanation: The source traces Tesla's initial guidance above $11 billion, its April 2025 revision above $10 billion, and actual 2025 spending of $8.527 billion. Actual spending missed both prepublication amounts, so the each-company antecedent was not met.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Under the stated each-company contract, the failed antecedent ends adjudication. An aggregate-condition reading would require a new contract and aligned spending and AI-revenue records for all five companies.
